# Introduction
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import seaborn as sns

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')
sns.set_context('talk')
```
The MSHB program is interested in looking at the seaborn dataset "Iris". 
This project will use python and quarto to examine the dataset by using correlation analysis.  

# Literature Review
We will com bacnk to LR. 

# Method
Given that we have two columns of continuous data(length of petal and width of petal measured in millimeters).
We will evaluate this relationship using simple correlation analysis and also a scatterplot. These methods are classic and traditional starting points when evaluating data like these. 

# Results
```{python}
corr_val = np.array(df[['petal_length', 'petal_width']].corr())[0][1]

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

if corr_val > .8:
 narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > .4: 
 narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
 narrative = "a positive but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -.4: 
 narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"
```
Using the class simple Pearson correlationship approach these data produce a correlation coefficient of `{python} f"{corr_val:.5f}"`. Given this result, we conclude that the relationship `{python}f"{narrative}"`.

```{python}
#| label: fig-length-width-scatter
#| fig-cap: "A scatterplot of petal length and width"

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))

sns.scatterplot(data=df, y = 'petal_length', x = 'petal_width')

plt.ylabel('Patal Width (mm)')
plt.xlabel('Patal Length (mm)')

```

As shown in @ fig-length-width-scatter we see additional evidence of a strong positive correlation between petal_length and petal_width.
